crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Routing Across Automated Market Makers
children.blurb: Routing across automated market makers is the practice of choosing and sequencing trades across multiple liquidity pools rather than sending an order to a single pool.

children.name: Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Yield strategies in smart contracts cover onchain methods for earning a return on crypto assets by placing them into decentralised finance protocols.

children.name: On-Chain Forensics
children.blurb: On-chain forensics is the practice of tracing activity on public blockchains to identify who moved what, when, and why.

children.name: Stablecoin Stress Testing
children.blurb: Stablecoin stress testing covers the set of analyses that ask how a stablecoin's peg, reserves and redemption process behave under adverse conditions.

children.name: Governance Token Outcomes
children.blurb: Governance token outcomes are the results that follow votes, delegation and proposal execution in token based communities.

sections.body: Crypto markets and decentralised finance are markets where trades settle on public blockchains and rules are written in smart contracts. Artificial intelligence is now used to choose trade routes across automated market makers, to adjust yield strategies in smart contracts, to trace funds on-chain, to stress test stablecoins, and to study governance token outcomes. In routing, bots compare pools, fees, slippage, and gas to split an order across venues. In yield work, models scan lending markets and liquidity pools for rates, incentives, and risk signals. In forensics, machine learning clusters addresses and flags suspicious flows for human review. These systems run in production, but they operate inside adversarial markets where other bots react to them.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are relatively settled. Routing has mature tooling, though it still fails when liquidity vanishes, gas spikes, or a private order flow channel changes the game. Yield strategies are harder, because backtests often overfit and live results depend on contract bugs, oracle failures, impermanent loss, and MEV. On-chain forensics can trace many flows, but mixers, bridges, privacy tools, and false positives limit certainty. Stablecoin stress testing can model redemption runs, yet reserves, counterparty exposure, and reflexive panic are often opaque. Governance token analysis can forecast votes and delegation shifts, but plutocratic control, low turnout, and legal ambiguity make outcomes unstable. The honest limit is that no model captures every regime change or black swan.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section divide the work by question. Routing Across Automated Market Makers is for execution and pathfinding, the mechanics of splitting an order and paying fees. Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts is for return seeking and the risks that come with lending, borrowing, and liquidity provision. On-Chain Forensics is for tracing, attribution, and compliance work after funds move. Stablecoin Stress Testing is for systemic risk, redemption pressure, and the stability of pegged assets. Governance Token Outcomes is for voting, delegation, and the incentives that shape protocol control. A reader can start with routing for trade mechanics, move to yield for strategy design, then use forensics, stablecoin stress, and governance pages to understand risk, tracing, and control.
